# Theme studio on the website

Status: Completed

A user-guide page where a person starts from a built-in theme or their own file, edits every field of a launcher theme with a live preview drawn by the site's instrument components, sees contrast hints, and downloads a JSON file the launcher reads.

## Scope

- In: Built-in themes exported from the Rust catalog to web/src/data/themes.generated.json, guarded by a lumilio-ui test
- In: Theme studio page in both languages under docs/guide, full width
- In: Editing: presets, import, several themes per file, colours (picker and hex with opacity), radii, fonts, window background, source
- In: Preview with the site's instrument components re-coloured through scoped CSS variables
- In: Validation with the launcher's rules, contrast hints, JSON download and copy, a local draft
- In: Shared instrument and font stylesheets split out of global.css; a guard that tokens.css matches the built-in themes
- Out: Rendering the real launcher in the browser
- Out: Uploading or sharing themes through the website
- Out: Launcher changes to the theme format

## Decision D1

The studio is a full-width page in the user guide, not a separate site page

Why: It inherits the documentation's language switch, search and navigation, next to the Themes page that explains the file.

Consequences: The page uses Starlight's splash template; its text lives in web/src/i18n/studio.ts.

## Decision D2

Built-in theme values come from Rust through a generated file, never copied by hand

Why: The launcher's catalog is the source of truth; a copy would drift as tokens.css already can.

Consequences: Changing a built-in theme requires refreshing the generated file, which the lumilio-ui test enforces.

## Decision D3

The preview re-colours the site's own instrument components instead of drawing a separate mock

Why: The marketing page already draws keys, LEDs and displays after the launcher's design language from CSS variables; setting those variables on the preview gives the same look from one stylesheet.

Consequences: Instrument styles move to a shared stylesheet. The preview is representative, not pixel-identical to the launcher.

## Decision D4

The launcher's contrast rules become one exported table

Why: The studio's hints must judge a theme as the launcher's own tests judge its built-in themes; a second copy in TypeScript would drift.

Consequences: Adding a rule in theme/tests/mod.rs reaches the studio after `just website-themes`; each rule id needs studio text in both languages, which model.test.ts enforces.

## Decision D5

radius is shown on fields and menus, radius_lg on dialogs and notifications; keys and panels keep fixed corners

Why: The launcher's own keys (key.rs) and panels use fixed radii; theme radii reach only gpui-component controls. The Themes guide said keys, which was wrong, and was corrected in the user-guide PR.

Consequences: The preview's keys never change shape with the radius sliders.

## Outcome

Added the theme studio to the user guide in both languages. Built-in themes, colour keys and contrast rules reach the website through a generated file that a lumilio-ui test keeps current, and a vitest guard keeps tokens.css equal to Aluminium and Night. The Project Maintainer reviewed the studio in a browser and loaded a downloaded theme in the launcher. The change merges after the user-guide PR; no deployment was performed.
